goal: Hook on the compelling question, then spot it and name it: the feelings faces chart gains its 1 to 5 strength scale (spot the body clue, name it, rate it), and a think-feel-do chain for a character whose classmate did not wave back adds what the character values, with "catch the thought, test it, try another"; every student tries each once.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. Before-you-teach note opens the unit. "Test it" is used on characters only; its look-for never asks a student to test their own thought aloud (Candidate kept, no day cost). No clinical words. Disclosure: health's steps (the school's reporting route and the counselor). Core link ela:e3-character-actions runs in the same weeks; the scene cards name the feeling and the action themselves. Supplies: the chart scale, the chain sheet, scene cards, printed.

goal: Pairs rehearse spot, name, rate on new school-day scene cards (a lost recess game, a hard spelling quiz) and fill a chain for a card character, the value step included, the card held by pairs.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to stop-think-choose with its card. Pairs swap roles each card; the teacher circulates with the look-fors.

goal: Card withdrawn: on an unseen scene card each student names a character's feeling, its clue and strength, says how what the character values helps explain the thought, and writes a second thought that fits the facts.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the calm-down plan card with its card. Seen against the look-fors with a written note for each student; not scored today.

goal: Calm it, calm-down first: the calm-down steps grow to four (stop, breathe, name it, choose) on a plan card with three body tools (slow breaths, a stretch, counting back from ten) for two school moments, a reason for each step; then the four steps before acting when a teammate grabs the ball, and reacting told apart from responding.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. Body tools done standing beside desks with room to reach, plain body skills with no spiritual framing (safety read). The plan card's three body tools are the same as health 3 to 5's calm tools, so one card serves both (Candidate kept, no day cost). The daily week of plan-card rehearsal starts today: the carry-out cue "stop, breathe, name it, choose" before transitions. Supplies: the plan card, printed.

goal: Pairs rehearse the four calm-down steps with a chosen body tool on school-moment cards, and say in one sentence how responding differs from reacting.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to naming a feeling and its strength with its card. Beside desks, room to reach. Pairs hold the card.

goal: Card withdrawn: each student fills their plan card for two new school moments and runs the four steps with a partner on an unseen moment card.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the think-feel-do chain with its card. The plan card is seen with written feedback today and revised before the Check (day 10); never scored on the day it is first made.

goal: Choose with care: stop-think-choose grows to four steps (stop, list two or three choices, think what each would cause, choose and check), shown on two invented classmates doing the same task, one who rushed and one who used the steps; then two options for a recess choice weighed for one's own and others' well-being; every student tries the card once.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. This card is used by units 2, 3 and 5. Supplies: the four-step stop-think-choose card, printed.

goal: Pairs rehearse the four stop-think-choose steps on new school-day choice cards, saying what each choice would cause and one place at home the steps would help.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the calm-down plan card with its card. Pairs hold the card.

goal: Card withdrawn: each student weighs the recess choice (finish a game indoors, or play with a classmate who is alone) for self and others and picks with a reason; then about half the pairs rehearse the four calm-down steps from an unseen card.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the four calm-down steps before acting with its card. End-of-unit rehearsal marks begin with the second half of the session. The weighed choice gets a written note and is revised in the Check's first minutes.

goal: End-of-unit assessment: an unseen scene page (a character's feeling, clue and strength; how the character's value explains the thought and feeling; a second thought that fits the facts; the step a character skipped) and the four calm-down steps rehearsed from an unseen card.

goal: Hook on the compelling question, then who I am: an identity web for an invented character (a team, a helper role at home, a club, a language) in three steps (list the groups, say what each adds, say where each part shows), and a strengths hunt in three steps (recall a task that went well, name the skill, find another place it helps) for a story character, a spoken language counting as a strength.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. The private interest log starts today and runs two weeks (what the student chose to do in free time, and why); it stays with the student. Model webs checked for range: families of every kind, a home language, a helper role (Candidate kept, no day cost). A student may make a private web of their own, or make one up; family and culture are never asked about by name. Core link: social studies grade 3 meets social-studies:ss3-biography across the year; the strengths hunt uses an invented character and needs nothing from it. Sensitivity read first studies an education association's guidance on families and cultures. Leave-out bridge: where unit 1 was left out, the first ten minutes teach four-step stop-think-choose.

goal: Pairs rehearse the web's three steps on a second invented character and the strengths hunt for a story character, each strength backed by an example.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to stop-think-choose with its card. Pairs hold the web and hunt cards.

goal: Second rehearsal: pairs swap model webs, say where each part shows, and back two more strengths with examples.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to naming a feeling and its strength with its card. Fold-in day on a short year (Shorter path).

goal: Card withdrawn: each student builds a web for a new invented character (or a private web of their own if they choose) and backs two strengths with examples.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the calm-down plan card with its card. Web and strengths seen with a written note; revised before the Check. A private web is checked only that the steps were followed.

goal: What I stand for and bring: the honest action on a school-day case (a classmate's answer sheet left in view) chosen with stop-think-choose, its value named and what honesty cost and kept; one entry picked from the private log and a purpose named; a three-part shout-out (what, how, why it mattered) after a planned partner task, and a vague "good job" rewritten.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. Carry-out cue starts: three-part shout-outs at the end of group work.

goal: Pairs rehearse three-part shout-outs after a short partner task and the honest choice on a new school-day case card.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to weighing well-being for me and others with its card. Pairs hold the shout-out card.

goal: Second rehearsal: shout-outs with a new partner, and two vague praise lines rewritten into three parts aloud.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the think-feel-do chain with its card. Fold-in day on a short year (Shorter path). Pairs hold the shout-out card.

goal: Card withdrawn: after a planned partner task each student gives a three-part shout-out; the honest choice on a new case with its value; the log closes with a purpose named privately; about half the pairs rehearse a shout-out from an unseen task card.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to stop-think-choose with its card. End-of-unit rehearsal marks begin. The log closes today, two weeks after day 12.

goal: Hook on the compelling question, then reading others: three kinds of clue (face, body, voice) read in short teacher-acted school scenes, the strength rated and the guess checked with a question; the shoes switch on a scene card (what each saw, wants and why each acted, then the scene retold from the other side); and three care steps (notice, ask what would help, do it) for a character who lost a library book.

goal: Pairs rehearse the care steps on new struggle cards (a dropped tray, a lost game piece) and read clues in teacher-acted scenes, each guess checked with a question.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to naming a feeling and its strength with its card. Pairs hold the care steps card; a partner plays only the low-stakes struggle on the card.

goal: Card withdrawn: on unseen scenes each student names three clues and a checking question, and retells a scene from the other side with that side's reason.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to stop-think-choose with its card. Seen with a written note.

goal: Checking my guess: a three-step check on a snap judgment (a quiet new student called stuck-up: catch the first thought, ask what I actually know, find out before deciding) with stop-think-choose; and with an invented story partner from another place on a shared class task, notice a different way, ask about it with respect, try it or combine it, the partner's way being a way of keeping score or taking turns in a game from home.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. The wrong guess rests on a neutral trait (quiet, new), never on skin, hair, dress, faith or accent; never blame of a group. The partner's game way is taken by the unit plan from a cited source the sensitivity agent reads first, not one of PE's, the arts' or K to 2's picks (Candidate kept, no day cost). No student is asked to explain their own culture.

goal: Pairs rehearse the three-step snap-judgment check on new neutral-trait cases and the respectful question to the story partner.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the shoes switch with its card. Pairs hold both cards.

goal: Card withdrawn: a shared class task played the story partner's way and the class's way, the respectful question asked and a combined way tried; one unseen snap-judgment case checked in writing.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to reading face, body and voice clues with its card. Seen with a written note.

goal: Thanks and systems: each gratitude note names the act, the person and the difference it made, and why noticing good things changes a class; one school system (the lunch line) followed in three steps (the rule, what it makes people do, what would happen without it).
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. goal: Pairs rehearse three-part gratitude notes for the wall and trace a second system (the bus line-up) with the three steps.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the care steps with its card. Pairs hold the system card.

goal: Card withdrawn: each student traces an unseen school system and adds a gratitude note to the wall; about half the pairs rehearse the care steps from an unseen card with the teacher playing the one who struggles.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the snap-judgment check with its card. End-of-unit rehearsal marks begin. The gratitude wall closes today, two weeks after day 22.

goal: Hook on the compelling question, then talk it out and repair, in this order: the talk turn card grows to four steps (listen, say back what you heard, ask a question, add your idea) in a planned partner talk; the I-statement grows to four parts ("I feel ___ when ___ because ___. I need ___.") with "cool, talk, choose" and a fair solution picked from two; and a broken-trust moment repaired in three steps (own it, say sorry with the I-statement, make a plan).
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine, then one retrieval item per sub-skill on its grade 2 form, a scenario item at the earlier depth; on a miss the earlier step is modeled again. goal: Pairs rehearse the talk turn card and the four-part I-statement on recess disagreement cards, both partners saying an I-statement.
note: Opening (5 min): calm-down routine and a three-minute return to the four calm-down steps before acting with its card. Fold-in day on a short year (Shorter path). Ordinary low-stakes disagreements where both sides are fair; pairs hold the cards.

goal: Hook on the compelling question, then think ahead and hold my ground: what each of two choices causes next, later that day and next week, with stop-think-choose; a four-step refusal (stop and think, say no clearly, give a reason, offer something else or walk away) and why a reason makes a no stronger; and an upstander plan with four options (speak up with an I-statement, stand with the one left out, get help, check in after).
